body:
I ran some tests to verify the behavior of `beforeunload` and `unload` events in some of the major browsers. The test involves loading an `<embed>` with some HTML content which has both `beforeunload` and `unload` handlers and examining whether or not either of the handlers are called when the content is _somehow_ removed.The results are summarized below (test [page](https://ehsan-karamad.github.io/embed_tests.html) for verification).

| Browser | Version | `beforeunload` | `unload` |
|---------|---------|:------------:|:----------:|
|Google Chrome | 65.0.3325.181 | always<sup>1</sup> | always<sup>2</sup> |
|Firefox Quantum | 59.0.2 |  close tab, navigate `window`<sup>3</sup> | always |
|Microsoft Edge |38.14393.2068.0|navigate `window` | navigate `window`|
|Safari |  5.1.10 | close tab, navigate `window`| delete `embed`, close tab, navigate `window`|

<sup>1</sup> Always for `beforeunload` includes: changing attributes, closing tab, and navigating window (of the `embed` exposed through `postMessage`). Note that changing `type` and `src` seems to only work (be supported by) Chrome and Firefox. On MS Edge and Safari, after attaching an `embed`, changing its `src` and `type` seems to have no effect. 

<sup>2</sup> Always for `unload` includes all the cases for `beforeunload` plus detaching the element.

<sup>3</sup> Navigating the `window` object of the frame inside the `<ebmed>`. This is obtained from the `Event.source` using `postMessage`. On Chrome, Firefox, and Safari this is also accessible from `window.frames` in the embedder page.
